validated_results.title: Dietary carbohydrate intake and risks of overall and 21 site-specific cancers: a prospective cohort study.
validated_results.reason: This prospective UK Biobank cohort reports a fully adjusted hazard ratio for energy-adjusted dietary fiber intake and incident kidney cancer, matching the requested exposure, cancer, and incidence outcome.

extraction.comparison_type: per IQR increase in energy-adjusted fiber intake

sample_size.excerpt: We conducted a large population-based prospective cohort research based on the UK Biobank including 194,388 participants.

effect_size.excerpt: Energy-adjusted fiber was associated with a reduced risk of overall cancer [HR per IQR increase (95% CI): 0.97 (0.96, 0.99); PFDR : 0.045] and esophageal [0.79 (0.68, 0.91); 0.024], colorectal [0.92 (0.87, 0.97); 0.025], lung [0.87 (0.81, 0.94); 0.014], and kidney cancer [0.85 (0.76, 0.94); 0.031].

confidence_interval.excerpt: Energy-adjusted fiber was associated with a reduced risk of overall cancer [HR per IQR increase (95% CI): 0.97 (0.96, 0.99); PFDR : 0.045] and esophageal [0.79 (0.68, 0.91); 0.024], colorectal [0.92 (0.87, 0.97); 0.025], lung [0.87 (0.81, 0.94); 0.014], and kidney cancer [0.85 (0.76, 0.94); 0.031].

design.excerpt: We conducted a large population-based prospective cohort research based on the UK Biobank

timing.excerpt: with a median follow-up of 12.8 years

exposure_measurement.excerpt: The Oxford WebQ, a web-based 24-h recall questionnaire, was used to collect dietary information

extraction.p_value_method: two-sided Wald test from effect and 95% CI on the log scale
extraction.ethnicity_basis: NA: no field-specific ethnicity evidence was available
